sentences.en: In the contentious fight over how to address climate change in the United States, recycled lead is a feel-good story.
sentences.zh: 在关于如何应对美国气候变化的争论中，再生铅是一个感觉良好的故事。

sentences.en: It can be processed with techniques that keep workers safe and reused in batteries that power millions of vehicles around the world.
sentences.zh: 它可以采用保护工人安全的技术进行加工，并重新用于为全球数百万辆汽车提供动力的电池中。

sentences.en: But a New Times investigation reveals how this environmental initiative comes at a major human coSt.
sentences.zh: 但《纽约时报》的一项调查揭示了这一环保倡议背后沉重的人类代价。

sentences.en: Today, Peter Goodman explains the dirty business of a supposedly clean technology.
sentences.zh: 今天，彼得·古德曼将解释这种所谓的清洁技术背后肮脏的生意。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, December 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月2日，星期二。

sentences.en: Peter, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 彼得，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: You are one of our foremost experts on the global economy.
sentences.zh: 你是我们全球经济领域的顶尖专家之一。

sentences.en: And you just came out with this really eye-opening investigation on recycled batteries and lead poisoning, which I will bet is not something that most people know a lot about.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚发表了这份关于再生铅电池和铅中毒的、令人大开眼界的调查，我敢打赌，大多数人对此并不十分了解。

sentences.en: So I'm very curious to know two things.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常好奇两件事。

sentences.en: One, how did you even get on this investigation?
sentences.zh: 第一，你是怎么开始这项调查的？

sentences.en: And number two, how much did you, Peter, know about recycled batteries when you first started?
sentences.zh: 第二，彼得，你刚开始时对再生电池了解多少？

sentences.en: I knew zero about recycled batteries.
sentences.zh: 我对其一无所知。

sentences.en: And that's rounding up.
sentences.zh: 而且这还是往多了说。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So I got a call from a guy at the examination, which is this relatively new independent investigative newsroom that specializes in global public health.
sentences.zh: 我接到了一位来自The Examination工作人员的电话，这是一个相对较新的独立调查新闻机构，专门报道全球公共卫生。

sentences.en: And they have this really terrific reporter, a guy I'd never met, though I'd heard about him,
sentences.zh: 他们有一位非常优秀的记者，一个我从未见过但听说过的人，

sentences.en: Will Fitzgibbon.
sentences.zh: 威尔·菲茨吉本。

sentences.en: He had done a fair bit of work already in Africa.
sentences.zh: 他在非洲已经做了相当多的工作。

sentences.en: He was a lead expert.
sentences.zh: 他是一位铅专家。

sentences.en: He dug into the lead recycling industry.
sentences.zh: 他深入研究了铅回收行业。

sentences.en: And this is the industry that supplies a lot of the car batteries that we find under the hoods of cars in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这就是为我们在美国汽车引擎盖下找到的大量汽车电池提供原材料的行业。

sentences.en: We're talking new cars, used cars, places like AutoZone, Home Depot, Walmart.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是新车、二手车，还有AutoZone、全国家居建材和沃尔玛这样的地方。

sentences.en: And a lot of the lead that we're using to make car batteries in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们在美国用来制造汽车电池的很多铅，

sentences.en: is coming from outside of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 都是从美国境外进口的，

sentences.en: because we've run out of supply domestically.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的国内供应已经耗尽。

sentences.en: So the industry's gone out looking around the world for new sources of lead.
sentences.zh: 所以该行业一直在世界各地寻找新的铅来源。

sentences.en: And one of the places it's now looking quite aggressively is Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 它现在正积极寻找的其中一个地方就是尼日利亚。

sentences.en: Will had already spent a fair bit of time looking into what this business actually looks like on the ground.
sentences.zh: 威尔已经花了不少时间调查这项业务在实地的真实情况。

sentences.en: He'd already figured out that the process of recycling lead was being done in a way that was really quite horrific to see up close.
sentences.zh: 他已经发现，铅的回收过程对近距离目睹的人来说简直是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: It was really harmful to people.
sentences.zh: 它对人们造成了极大的伤害。

sentences.en: And he'd have this terrific idea, which was that, you know, we would actually go and test people.
sentences.zh: 他有个绝妙的主意，那就是去对人们进行检测。

sentences.en: We would find people willing to volunteer for blood tests and quantify just exactly how much lead was reaching people's bloodstreaMs.
sentences.zh: 我们会找到愿意自愿进行血液检测的人，并精确量化有多少铅进入了人们的血流。

sentences.en: And we'd also test soil to look into the tainting of the food supply.
sentences.zh: 我们还将检测土壤，以查明食品供应是否受到污染。

sentences.en: And so I got enlisted to try to take a run at figuring out who was buying it, how the terms of trade were going down, all the logistics along the way.
sentences.zh: 所以我被招募来试图弄清楚是谁在购买、贸易条款是如何达成的，以及沿途的所有物流。

sentences.en: They wanted me because I've been writing versions of complex supply chain stories now for 25 plus years around the world.
sentences.zh: 他们找我是因为我25年多来一直在世界各地撰写各种复杂的供应链故事。

sentences.en: And I didn't know anything about this particular industry, but I did have some inkling about shipping, logistics.
sentences.zh: 我对这个特定行业一无所知，但我对航运和物流确实有一些了解。

sentences.en: And I was certainly intrigued to try to make the connection between this public health catastrophe in West Africa and the auto industry in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我当然很想把西非的这场公共卫生灾难与美国的汽车产业联系起来。

sentences.en: That connection sounds incredibly challenging to make.
sentences.zh: 建立这种联系听起来极具挑战性。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's enormously challenging, especially because we're talking about a trade that's secret.
sentences.zh: 是的，挑战巨大，特别是这是一项秘密贸易。

sentences.en: I mean, the participants have no interest in talking to anybody about this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，参与者根本没有兴趣跟任何人谈论这些事。

sentences.en: There's limited publicly available data.
sentences.zh: 公开可用的数据非常有限。

sentences.en: And so I found myself taking on what, quite honestly, was the most difficult reporting assignment of my career.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现自己接手了说实话是我职业生涯中最困难的报道任务。

sentences.en: Where did you actually start the reporting journey?
sentences.zh: 你实际上是在哪里开始这段报道之旅的？

sentences.en: So Will had already done a lot of this legwork.
sentences.zh: 威尔已经做了很多这样的前期准备工作。

sentences.en: He already had sources in Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 他在尼日利亚已经有了消息源。

sentences.en: He understood where these factories were.
sentences.zh: 他了解这些工厂在哪里。

sentences.en: And then I went there with Will to nail down the real life consequences for the people living
sentences.zh: 然后我和威尔一起去那里，去确定生活在这些工厂隔壁村庄里的人们所面临的现实生活影响，

sentences.en: in villages right next to these plants and also to go talk to people in Lagos who could tell
sentences.zh: 也去拉各斯与一些人交谈，他们可以告诉我们有关尼日利亚供应链的部分，

sentences.en: us about the Nigeria supply chain part of it before this lead gets put into shipping containers and sent across the water for ports around the world.
sentences.zh: 然后这些铅会被装进货运集装箱，运过水面送往世界各地的港口。

sentences.en: So where exactly did you go and what did you see there?
sentences.zh: 那你具体去了哪里？你在那里看到了什么？

sentences.en: So I went to a place called Ogijo, which is just north of Lagos, which is a sprawling, you know, enormous metropolitan area.
sentences.zh: 我去了奥吉乔（Ogijo）这个地方，它位于拉各斯正北方，那是一个庞大无比的大都市区。

sentences.en: And Ogijo is sort of a combination of an industrial and rural where there are a bunch of smelters, including the one that we wound up focusing on called True Metals.
sentences.zh: 奥吉乔有点像是工业区和农村的结合体，那里有一堆冶炼厂，包括我们最终重点关注的那家名为“真实金属”（True Metals）的工厂。

sentences.en: And we picked it not only because it's really bad in terms of the pollution that it puts out, but also because it only deals in lead.
sentences.zh: 我们选择它不仅因为它排放的污染非常严重，还因为它只经营铅业务。

sentences.en: And these are large factories where people are feeding this lead into these giant furnaces
sentences.zh: 这些大型工厂里人们把铅送进巨大的熔炉，

sentences.en: villages that send smoke wafting throughout the area, including in these villages that are right next to the factories.
sentences.zh: 村庄里烟雾缭绕，甚至弥漫在紧邻工厂的村子里。

sentences.en: So I spent a lot of time just sitting with families, talking to them about the struggle of living next door to these plants.
sentences.zh: 所以我花了很多时间与家庭坐在一起，和他们谈论住在这些工厂隔壁的艰难生活。

sentences.en: People were coughing.
sentences.zh: 人们在咳嗽。

sentences.en: People were complaining of all sorts of ailments that are linked in the literature to lead poisoning,
sentences.zh: 人们抱怨各种文献中与铅中毒有关的病痛，

sentences.en: you know, indigestion and various gastrointestinal distress, unrelenting headaches.
sentences.zh: 比如消化不良、各种肠胃不适以及挥之不去的头痛。

sentences.en: And I saw children in schools that were literally next to these factories.
sentences.zh: 我看到孩子们在紧挨着这些工厂的学校里上学。

sentences.en: So I was just blown away and really horrified by what I was seeing up close.
sentences.zh: 所以我亲眼看到这一切后感到震惊和无比惊骇。

sentences.en: And it gave me a real sense of the story is really important.
sentences.zh: 这让我真切地意识到这个故事非常重要。

sentences.en: So what you're seeing in this town is all these signs of pollution that is coming from this lead battery recycling process.
sentences.zh: 所以你在小镇上看到的所有这些污染迹象都来自这个铅电池回收过程。

sentences.en: Before we get any further in the story, I just want to have you explain how and why a battery
sentences.zh: 在我们进一步深入这个故事之前，我想请你解释一下，电池是如何以及为什么要以正确的方式进行回收的，然后你在尼日利亚看到了什么，以及它有什么不同。

sentences.en: gets recycled the correct way and then what you saw in Nigeria and how that was different.
sentences.zh: 嗯，需要指出的是，路上几乎每辆车下面某处都有一个铅酸电池，甚至电动汽车也是如此。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's important to note that virtually every car on the road has a lead battery under there somewhere, even electric vehicles.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有铅酸电池，我们很快就会察觉到。

sentences.en: And if we didn't have lead batteries, we'd notice real faSt.
sentences.zh: 碰巧这也是地球上可回收利用率最高的元素之一。

sentences.en: And it happens to be one of the most recyclable elements on earth.
sentences.zh: 汽车行业在将自己宣传为循环经济的典范时，确实倾向于这一点。

sentences.en: And the auto industry has really leaned into that in promoting itself as the exemplar of the circular economy.
sentences.zh: 他们确实回收了大部分旧电池，并且拥有非常先进的回收工厂。

sentences.en: They do recycle most of these old batteries and have very sophisticated plants that recycle.
sentences.zh: 他们有自动化流程来拆解旧电池并安全提取铅。

sentences.en: They have, you know, automated processes that break apart the old batteries and extract the lead safely.
sentences.zh: 他们处理里面的酸液。

sentences.en: They dispose of the acid that's in there.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有防止铅尘和烟雾喷涌到社区的排放控制设施。

sentences.en: They have emissions controls that prevent lead dust and smoke from spewing out into communities.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西都要花数百万美元。

sentences.en: All that stuff costs millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着美国等地法规越来越严格，我们的冶炼厂已经搬迁。

sentences.en: And so as regulations have gotten stricter in places like the United States, we've had smelters move.
sentences.zh: 这就消除了本地供应。

sentences.en: So that's eliminated local supply.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，随着人口增长，需求也在增加。

sentences.en: At the same time, demand is increased because population's growing.
sentences.zh: 开车的人越来越多了。

sentences.en: We got more people driving around in cars.
sentences.zh: 因此，电池制造商不得不走遍世界各地去寻找更多的铅。

sentences.en: And so battery manufacturers have had to go around the world to go find more lead.
sentences.zh: 我在尼日利亚看到的情景，与如果你有幸被邀请进入北美铅回收厂时看到的情景截然不同。

sentences.en: And what I saw in Nigeria was something very different than what you would see if you managed to get invited into a lead recycling plant in North America.
sentences.zh: 首先，我看到人们在所谓的拆解场里工作。

sentences.en: I saw, first of all, people in so-called breaking yards.
sentences.zh: 这些地方是他们获取废旧电池的地方。

sentences.en: These are the places where they get the spent batteries.
sentences.zh: 这些电池是由被称为拾荒者的人带来的，他们开着三轮车、自行车、摩托车或卡车前来。

sentences.en: They're brought by these people known as pickers who come in by rickshaw, bicycle, motorbike,
sentences.zh: 他们把旧电池带到这些场子里。

sentences.en: truck.
sentences.zh: 然后，通常光着膀子、没有任何防护装备的男人们用大砍刀砸开塑料外壳。

sentences.en: And they bring these old batteries into these yards.
sentences.zh: 就是不停地捶打它们。

sentences.en: And then men, often shirtless with no protective gear whatsoever, use machetes to break apart the plastic cases.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Just hammering at them.
sentences.zh: 在美国，这本该是在严密控制的环境下由机器完成的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is what would have been done by machines in the United States in a tightly controlled environment.
sentences.zh: 这听起来极其危险。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 极其危险。

sentences.en: This sounds incredibly dangerous.
sentences.zh: 你光凭直觉就能感觉到。

sentences.en: Incredibly dangerous.
sentences.zh: 比如，你不需要拥有环境科学博士学位也能明白，不戴护目镜、不戴手套、光着膀子，拿着大砍刀猛砸旧电池、让酸液朝四面八方喷溅，绝对不是个好主意。

sentences.en: You can just sense it.
sentences.zh: 规模较小的作坊会把酸液直接倾倒进水道里。

sentences.en: Like, you don't need some sort of PhD in environmental science to understand that it's not a good idea
sentences.zh: 简直骇人听闻。

sentences.en: to have no safety goggles, to have no gloves, to not have a shirt on, to be taking a machete, slamming it into an old battery with acid spewing out in every direction.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The smaller operations, they take the acid and they actually dump it into waterways.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是电池拆解作业。

sentences.en: It's just horrifying.
sentences.zh: 接下来是熔炉。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 这是绝大部分污染的来源。

sentences.en: So that's just the battery breaking operations.
sentences.zh: 熔炉是那些巨大的设施，它们将从废旧电池中取出的旧铅熔化。

sentences.en: Then there's the furnaces.
sentences.zh: 它们在极高的温度下将其煮沸成熔融液体，然后倒入模具中形成锭块，接着就可以转运到制造新电池的电池制造商那里。

sentences.en: This is where most of the pollution comes from.
sentences.zh: 如果你在美国看到一家工厂或一座熔炉，你会看到用来吸尘的设备。

sentences.en: And the furnaces are these giant facilities that take the old lead taken out of spent batteries and they melt it down.
sentences.zh: 你会看到防止烟雾外泄到社区的机械装置。

sentences.en: They cook it at incredibly high temperatures into this molten liquid that's poured into molds that then form these ingots that can then be, you know, moved around, trucked
sentences.zh: 你会看到各种自动化系统，以防止工人们赤手触碰物品而导致自己中毒。

sentences.en: to battery manufacturers that make new batteries.
sentences.zh: 我在尼日利亚看到的完全是露天的。

sentences.en: And if you saw a plant, a furnace in the U.S., you'd see equipment used to vacuum up duSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以亲眼看到烟雾从工厂屋顶的瓦楞铁皮缝隙间冒出来。

sentences.en: You'd see machinery that prevents smoke from getting out into the communities.
sentences.zh: 你能闻到它的气味。

sentences.en: You'd see all sorts of automated systems to prevent workers from poisoning themselves by touching things with their bare hands.
sentences.zh: 我被邀请进入人们的家中。

sentences.en: What I saw in Nigeria was just open air.
sentences.zh: 我跟一个男人交谈过，他说，是的，我的墙壁都是黑的。

sentences.en: I mean, you could see the smoke with your bare eyes just getting out between the sheets of corrugated metal that are the roofs of these factories.
sentences.zh: 你也能亲眼看到。

sentences.en: You could smell it.
sentences.zh: 烟雾实在太浓烈了。

sentences.en: I was invited into people's homes.
sentences.zh: 这种影响如此明显、如此真切，让人不可能无动于衷。

sentences.en: I talked to a man who said, yeah, my walls are black.
sentences.zh: 听起来这些地方是在几乎没有任何监管的情况下运营的。

sentences.en: And you could see it.
sentences.zh: 你是如何追踪他们生产的铅的去向的？

sentences.en: Just the smoke is so intense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们有贸易数据。

sentences.en: And the impacts of this are just so obvious and so palpable that it was impossible to not be moved by this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，The Examination的威尔建立了一个包含所有公开可用信息的极棒的数据库。

sentences.en: So it sounds like these places are operating with very little regulation.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，贸易公司会确定世界各地再生铅的来源。

sentences.en: How did you end up tracing what happens to the lead that they produce?
sentences.zh: 他们会购买它。

sentences.en: Well, we had trade data.
sentences.zh: 他们会将其运往美国的终点，通常是巴尔的摩港。

sentences.en: You know, Will, at the examination, built a terrific database that had all the publicly available information.
sentences.zh: 然后故事就断了。

sentences.en: So typically, a trading company will identify sources of recycled lead around the world.
sentences.zh: 所以我的工作就是弄清楚，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: They'll buy it.
sentences.zh: 那你具体是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: They'll ship it to an endpoint in the United States, typically the port of Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 我很快发现没有专家可打电话咨询。

sentences.en: And then the story ended.
sentences.zh: 没有人写过关于这个的学位论文。

sentences.en: So my job was to figure out, well, then what happens?
sentences.zh: 没有任何书籍。

sentences.en: So how did you do that?
sentences.zh: 也没有YouTube纪录片可以看作参考。

sentences.en: So I quickly figured out there's no expert to call.
sentences.zh: 甚至连Reddit上都没有那些靠不住的内幕消息。

sentences.en: There's nobody who did a dissertation on this.
sentences.zh: 我当时完全一头雾水……

sentences.en: There's no book.
sentences.zh: 哦，Reddit上什么都有。

sentences.en: There's no YouTube documentaries to watch for tips.
sentences.zh: 对，但当时这完全是个黑箱。

sentences.en: There isn't even, you know, Reddit to go get dubious, you know, tips.
sentences.zh: 我开始联系那些在这些贸易公司工作的人。

sentences.en: I was juSt...
sentences.zh: 我们想要看看下一颗星星的外面是什么。

sentences.en: Oh, Reddit for everything.
sentences.zh: 噢，什么事都上 Reddit。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was just a black box.
sentences.zh: 对，它就像是一个黑盒。

sentences.en: And I started to reach out to people who worked for these trading companies.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始联系那些在这些贸易公司工作的人。

sentences.en: The one I was most focused on was this company called Trafigura.
sentences.zh: 我最关注的是一家名为托克（Trafigura）的公司。

sentences.en: And to be clear, Trafigura is basically a middleman here.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，托克在这里基本上扮演中间商的角色。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Trafigura's job is to buy and sell commodities.
sentences.zh: 托克的工作是买卖大宗商品。

sentences.en: They're the ones who are most expert in what's available, what's the price.
sentences.zh: 他们最精通什么货源可用、价格是多少。

sentences.en: And so we had transactions we could see in the database where Trafigura is buying lead from these smelters we're focusing on in Nigeria and shipping it to the port of Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在数据库中看到了这样的交易记录：托克向我们在尼日利亚重点关注的这些冶炼厂购买铅，并将其运往巴尔的摩港。

sentences.en: But I had no idea who was buying it at that point.
sentences.zh: 但当时我根本不知道是谁在买它。

sentences.en: And so I did a bunch of different things.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了很多不同的事情。

sentences.en: I signed up to go to trade shows, hoping I would run into people who would help tell me the story.
sentences.zh: 我报名参加贸易展，希望能遇到能帮我讲述这个故事的人。

sentences.en: I spent a lot of time on LinkedIn, just mass messaging anybody who had worked at Trafigura.
sentences.zh: 我在领英上花了很多时间，向所有在托克工作过的人群发消息。

sentences.en: And that was pretty lonely and felt fairly futile.
sentences.zh: 那段经历相当孤立，而且感觉挺徒劳的。

sentences.en: Most people ignored me.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都忽略了我。

sentences.en: Some sent me to the communications people who then ignored me.
sentences.zh: 有些人把我转给公关人员，然后公关人员也忽略了我。

sentences.en: Um, and then eventually a handful of people started helping me in a really critical way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，后来有几个人开始以非常关键的方式帮助我。

sentences.en: And they started to name the same likely purchaser over and over again.
sentences.zh: 他们开始一遍又一遍地指出同一个极有可能的买家。

sentences.en: They named East Penn, which is the second largest battery manufacturer in the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们说的是东彭（East Penn），美国第二大电池制造商。

sentences.en: It's this family owned business.
sentences.zh: 这是一家家族企业。

sentences.en: They're not publicly traded.
sentences.zh: 他们没有上市。

sentences.en: They're very quiet and, and they don't like to deal with the press.
sentences.zh: 他们非常低调，而且不喜欢跟媒体打交道。

sentences.en: And they certainly didn't want to deal with me.
sentences.zh: 他们当然也绝对不想跟我打交道。

sentences.en: So at this point, I know, and I put that in quotation marks, like I know on deep backgrounds, right,
sentences.zh: 所以到这个时候，我了解到了——我这里加了引号，就像我通过深度的背景调查了解到的那样，对吧，

sentences.en: with no names attached and no documents, that East Penn is buying lead from trading companies that are bringing it into the port of Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 没有署名也没有文件，东彭正在从把铅运到巴尔的摩港的贸易公司那里购买铅。

sentences.en: But I can't prove it.
sentences.zh: 但我无法证明这一点。

sentences.en: You can't report it yet.
sentences.zh: 你还不能报道。

sentences.en: I can't report it.
sentences.zh: 我没法报道。

sentences.en: Good reporting, but it's not reportable yet.
sentences.zh: 很好的调查，但现在还不到能报道的时候。

sentences.en: It's not, it's certainly not going to be a satisfying, significant part of the story based on that sourcing.
sentences.zh: 基于这些信源，它绝对不会成为这个故事中令人满意且重要的部分。

sentences.en: I needed something stronger.
sentences.zh: 我需要更有力的证据。

sentences.en: So I went to the port of Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了巴尔的摩港。

sentences.en: I actually spent a whole day there with a really excellent photographer who had probably the most unexciting day of her life.
sentences.zh: 我实际上在那里度过了一整天，陪同的还有一位非常优秀的摄影师，而这可能是她一生中最无趣的一天。

sentences.en: It was kind of a fairly futile day.
sentences.zh: 那可以说是相当徒劳的一天。

sentences.en: We actually chartered a little fishing boat, and we just, like, tooled around the harbor in Baltimore, and we were able to see the dock where some of these shipments come in.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至租了一艘小渔船，在巴尔的摩港闲逛，我们看到了其中一些货物运达的码头。

sentences.en: We saw a trucking yard where they unloaded from the water, and we got a sense of the geography, but there was no vessel bringing in lead on this particular day.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了一个他们从水上卸货的卡车停车场，我们对那里的地理情况有了一些概念，但在那特定的一天，并没有船只运送铅进来。

sentences.en: But I did learn something, and because of that reporting, because of what I learned at the truck yard,
sentences.zh: 但我确实学到了一些东西，因为那次实地调查，因为我在卡车停车场了解到的情况，

sentences.en: I reached out to this logistics company where a guy who ran the yard did very reluctantly and somewhat elliptically confirm that they handled lead incoming from West Africa,
sentences.zh: 我联系了一家物流公司，那里的一个停车场负责人非常勉强、含糊其辞地证实，他们确实处理过来自西非的进口铅，

sentences.en: purchased by Trafigura, and they sent some of it out to Pennsylvania to East Penn.
sentences.zh: 由托克采购，他们把其中一部分运到了宾夕法尼亚州的东彭。

sentences.en: But we still really needed to talk to East Penn about all this because, you know, let's remember, this is the second largest battery manufacturer in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但我们仍然真的需要就所有这些事情与东彭谈谈，因为，你知道，我们要记住，这是美国第二大电池制造商。

sentences.en: It's not a household name.
sentences.zh: 它并不是一个家喻户晓的名字。

sentences.en: It's not a company most of us ever think about, but it's there, and we're participants.
sentences.zh: 它不是我们大多数人会想到的公司，但它就在那里，而我们都是参与者。

sentences.en: They're making batteries under the hoods of millions of cars that are out there on the road.
sentences.zh: 他们正在为数百万行驶在路上的汽车引擎盖下制造电池。

sentences.en: They're the ones actually profiting off of this and depending upon the supply in Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 他们才是真正从中获利并依赖尼日利亚供应的人。

sentences.en: So I wanted to understand what sorts of due diligence they were undertaking to ensure that this lead they were buying from Nigeria was in compliance with their social and environmental standard.
sentences.zh: 所以我想要了解，他们究竟采取了什么样的尽职调查，来确保他们从尼日利亚购买的这些铅符合他们的社会和环境标准。

sentences.en: So I'd had calls out to East Penn, and they were just blowing me off.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直给东彭打电话，而他们完全在敷衍我。

sentences.en: They weren't responding to my calls.
sentences.zh: 他们不回我的电话。

sentences.en: I wasn't getting responses to my emails.
sentences.zh: 我的电子邮件也没有收到回复。

sentences.en: Just no response.
sentences.zh: 就是没有任何回复。

sentences.en: And it became clear to me that I was going to have to figure out how to confront East Penn.
sentences.zh: 我渐渐明白，我必须想办法去正面质问东彭。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘玟（Wena Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》（Connections）游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我也喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazurski, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基（Sam Mazurski），我每天都负责创作《拼写蜜蜂》（Spelling Bee）和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉（promesthesia）的状况。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始游玩。

sentences.en: Peter, I spent many years as a reporter, so I can absolutely relate to this idea that you have questions,
sentences.zh: 彼得，我当过多年记者，所以我绝对能感同身受这种感觉：你有疑问，

sentences.en: you have to get in front of the people you're writing about, give them an opportunity to respond, and you are getting nowhere trying to go in through the front door,
sentences.zh: 你必须面对面接触你所报道的对象，给他们一个回应的机会，然而你通过正门去沟通却处处碰壁，

sentences.en: which is what sounds like it was happening to you with East Penn.
sentences.zh: 听起来你对东彭的采访经历就是这样的。

sentences.en: So, I imagine you had to get creative about how to actually give them an opportunity to comment?
sentences.zh: 所以，我想你不得不发挥创意，想想怎么才能真正给他们一个置评的机会？

sentences.en: I had to make a spectacle of my show.
sentences.zh: 我不得不把我的节目搞成一场轰动全场的奇观。

sentences.en: Excellent.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: That's actually how it happened.
sentences.zh: 事实确实如此。

sentences.en: So, the big break was in San Antonio, where the Battery Council International has this gathering.
sentences.zh: 所以，重大的突破发生在圣安东尼奥，国际电池理事会（Battery Council International）在那里举办了一次聚会。

sentences.en: It's this big, you know, golf resort, and there are people from battery companies and lead recycling,
sentences.zh: 那是一个很大的、你知道的、高尔夫度假村，那里有来自电池公司、铅回收公司的人，

sentences.en: and, you know, companies that make equipment used, and they're all golfing and drinking and dining and having a good time.
sentences.zh: 还有那些制造所需设备的公司，你知道的，他们都在打高尔夫、喝酒、聚餐，过得很愉快。

sentences.en: And the second I identify what story I'm working on, they either don't know anything about it, because most people, when I would tell them the story, they'd say,
sentences.zh: 而我一旦确定了我正在调查的故事，他们要么一无所知，因为大多数人，当我把这个故事讲给他们听时，他们会说：

sentences.en: Nigeria, no way, we're not buying lead from Nigeria.
sentences.zh: “尼日利亚？不可能，我们绝不会从尼日利亚买铅。”

sentences.en: That's just not even possible.
sentences.zh: “这根本不可能。”

sentences.en: How could they even have lead?
sentences.zh: “他们怎么可能连铅都有？”

sentences.en: Wow, okay, they didn't even know.
sentences.zh: 哇，好吧，他们甚至对此一无所知。

sentences.en: And then the handful of people who did know were like, the last thing I want to do is talk about this subject with someone from the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 然后仅有的几个知情者则觉得：我最不想做的事，就是跟《纽约时报》的人谈论这个话题。

sentences.en: And I figured out that the head of East Penn, the then CEO of East Penn, this guy Chris Pruitt, is getting this Distinguished Service Award from the Battery Council International,
sentences.zh: 我发现东彭的负责人、当时的东彭首席执行官克里斯·普鲁伊特（Chris Pruitt）将获得国际电池理事会的杰出服务奖，

sentences.en: and I'm planning to go, because it's going to be my only shot.
sentences.zh: 我正计划去参加，因为这将是我唯一的成败机会。

sentences.en: At this point, I've got calls out to their various marketing people.
sentences.zh: 到了这个时候，我一直在给他们的各个营销人员打电话。

sentences.en: I've just gotten nowhere.
sentences.zh: 我完全碰壁了。

sentences.en: So, I know Chris Pruitt's there.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道克里斯·普鲁伊特在那儿。

sentences.en: I really want to talk to him.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想跟他谈谈。

sentences.en: The communications guy says, this is supposed to be honoring him, and if you're there asking these uncomfortable questions, that'll really be awkward.
sentences.zh: 公关人员说，这本该是向他致敬的表彰，如果你在那儿提出这些让人不舒服的问题，那真的会很尴尬。

sentences.en: Now, the reporter in me is like, well, I don't really care.
sentences.zh: 现在，我骨子里的记者本能觉得，好吧，我其实不在乎。

sentences.en: I work for the reader.
sentences.zh: 我为读者工作。

sentences.en: I have to go ask these questions.
sentences.zh: 我必须去问这些问题。

sentences.en: But I thought, well, if I'm not going to get anywhere anyway, and I'm just going to make a spectacle of myself, there's no upside to that.
sentences.zh: 但我想，好吧，反正我也无法取得进展，而且我只会让自己出丑，那样做没有任何好处。

sentences.en: You won't ambush him.
sentences.zh: 你不会去伏击他。

sentences.en: I won't ambush him, but out of that, I'll get some basis for a more productive engagement and maybe go visit him in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我不会去伏击他，但通过这件事，我可以为更有成效的接触奠定一些基础，也许还可以去宾夕法尼亚州拜访他。

sentences.en: I do finally hear from an outside PR firm for East Penn, and I start to engage with them.
sentences.zh: 我终于收到了东彭外部公关公司的消息，我开始与他们接触。

sentences.en: Eventually, I was able to persuade Chris Pruitt and other executives at East Penn to talk to us.
sentences.zh: 最终，我说服了克里斯·普鲁伊特和东彭的其他高管来和我们谈谈。

sentences.en: And what did he actually say to you?
sentences.zh: 他实际上对你说了什么？

sentences.en: Well, he said that our reporting had caused him to do a lot more thinking that he'd previously done about the origins of the lead,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他说我们的报道让他对铅的来源进行了比以往更多的思考，

sentences.en: and that previously he had talked to trading companies like Trafigura and had said, you know, I need this particular purity.
sentences.zh: 而且在此之前，他曾与托克等贸易公司交谈过，并说过，你知道的，我需要这种特定的纯度。

sentences.en: And, oh, by the way, of course you're guaranteeing that this is not causing social or environmental probleMs.
sentences.zh: 哦，顺便说一句，当然，你们要保证这不会引起社会或环境问题。

sentences.en: Oh, no, of course not.
sentences.zh: “哦，不，当然不会。”

sentences.en: The trading company would say, you know, we have audit processes.
sentences.zh: 贸易公司会说，你知道的，我们有审核流程。

sentences.en: You know, all this is good.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这一切都很好。

sentences.en: He said, okay, then, just as long as you can deliver the quantity and the purity that we need at the guaranteed price, all good.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，那么，只要你们能以保证的价格提供我们需要的数量和纯度，那就一切都好。

sentences.en: And since our reporting, he'd actually dug into his own supply chain, had become concerned about the process of due diligence that trading companies were doing.
sentences.zh: 自从我们的报道发表以来，他实际上深入调查了自己的供应链，开始对贸易公司正在做的尽职调查流程感到担忧。

sentences.en: And, as he put it, you know, out of the utmost of caution, decided that he didn't want to buy any more lead from Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 正如他所说，出于极其谨慎的考虑，他决定不想再从尼日利亚购买任何铅。

sentences.en: So, I did ask him at one point about moral culpability.
sentences.zh: 所以，我确实在某个时候问过他关于道德罪责的问题。

sentences.en: And I said, well, you know, given that we now know that Trafigura's due diligence leaves a lot to be desired,
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，你知道，鉴于我们现在知道托克的尽职调查远没有达到应有的水平，

sentences.en: and we could see with our own eyes and what was playing out in these villages next to these smelters, he said, where do you fit in terms of the moral culpability for this?
sentences.zh: 而且我们亲眼目睹了这些冶炼厂旁边的村庄里正在发生的事情，我说，对于这一切，你在道德罪责上处于什么位置？

sentences.en: And he said, he said, look, you know, was I too trusting?
sentences.zh: 他说，他说，听着，你知道的，我是不是太轻信了？

sentences.en: I'll take that shot.
sentences.zh: 我认栽。

sentences.en: What did you make of that?
sentences.zh: 你对这番话怎么看？

sentences.en: I thought that summed up the reality of complicated supply chains.
sentences.zh: 我认为这概括了复杂供应链的现实。

sentences.en: There's so much sort of plausible deniability built in that any given participant can say plausibly, oh, I thought somebody else was looking out.
sentences.zh: 其中内置了如此多的合理否认空间，以至于任何一个参与者都可以合情合理地说：“哦，我以为别人在盯着呢。”

sentences.en: Well, to that point, though, this is East Penn acknowledging that what's happening on the ground is not okay, right?
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这也是东彭承认实地发生的事情是不对的，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, it's not up to their standards as an American company.
sentences.zh: 就像，这不符合他们作为一家美国公司的标准。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But what about Trafigura?
sentences.zh: 但托克呢？

sentences.en: Like, have they made any kind of pledge to change or modify their behavior?
sentences.zh: 比如说，他们有没有做出任何改变或修正其行为的承诺？

sentences.en: So Trafigura gave us this kind of general statement,
sentences.zh: 所以托克给我们提供了这样一份笼统的声明，

sentences.en: but they say that they have an audit process that ensures that they're complying with their official social and environmental standards.
sentences.zh: 但他们说他们有一个审核流程，以确保他们遵守其官方的社会和环境标准。

sentences.en: And we actually talked to a consultant who does the audits for Trafigura in Lagos who pushed back on the idea that it's just, like, performative, superficial.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上和一位在拉各斯为托克做审核的顾问谈过，他反驳了这种审核仅仅是流于形式、表面的说法。

sentences.en: He said, I really go and I look.
sentences.zh: 他说，我真的会去实地查看。

sentences.en: First question I had is, okay, do you go to the battery-breaking yards?
sentences.zh: 我问的第一个问题是，好吧，你去过拆电池的场地吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No, I just go to the smelter.
sentences.zh: 没有，我只去冶炼厂。

sentences.en: Okay, so right off the bat,
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以开门见山地说，

sentences.en: you don't know anything about the raw materials that are coming in or the impacts for the people who are working in those places or where the acid's going.
sentences.zh: 你对进来的原材料、在这些地方工作的人们所受到的影响，或者酸液流向何处一无所知。

sentences.en: Is it going in a stream?
sentences.zh: 它是流进小溪里了吗？

sentences.en: You know, none of that, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些全都不了解，对吧？

sentences.en: So then even at the smelter, I said, well, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 所以即使在冶炼厂，我说，那你做什么？

sentences.en: He said, well, I look very, you know, carefully.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，我看得非常，你知道，仔细。

sentences.en: But the consultant said, I give them a real list of problems that I identify.
sentences.zh: 但这位顾问说，我确实给他们开出了一长串我发现的问题清单。

sentences.en: But the way this goes, and I confirmed this with people who've worked at Trafigura, is the auditor will say, okay, you know,
sentences.zh: 但事情的进展是这样的——我和在托克工作过的人确认过这一点——审核员会说，好吧，你知道，

sentences.en: it really would be good if you handed out safety goggles on a regular basis.
sentences.zh: 如果你能定期分发护目镜，那真的很好。

sentences.en: It really would be good if you put in a system to control the lead duSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你能建立一个控制铅尘的系统，那真的很好。

sentences.en: It would be great if you put in battery-breaking equipment.
sentences.zh: 如果你能引进拆电池设备，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: And the smelter will say, okay, thank you very much for your suggestion.
sentences.zh: 冶炼厂会说，好的，非常感谢您的建议。

sentences.en: We will certainly hand out safety goggles.
sentences.zh: 我们一定会分发护目镜。

sentences.en: And then Trafigura says, great, your audit's done.
sentences.zh: 然后托克说，太棒了，你们的审核完成了。

sentences.en: Now let's talk about the volume of the next deal.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来谈谈下一笔交易的货量吧。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not a process that can end up in derailing a deal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不是一个最终会导致交易告吹的流程。

sentences.en: This is a process that is informed by a desire to reach a conclusion at which the deal carries on.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由达成让交易得以继续的结论的愿望所驱动的流程。

sentences.en: And that's the problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: So there is due diligence.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有尽职调查。

sentences.en: There are inspections.
sentences.zh: 有检查。

sentences.en: There are recommendations.
sentences.zh: 有建议。

sentences.en: There are recommendations.
sentences.zh: 有建议。

sentences.en: There's an action plan.
sentences.zh: 有行动计划。

sentences.en: But there's no compulsion to do the right thing or the business doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但并没有强制要求去做正确的事，否则生意就做不成了。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, the person who's buying it on the other side of the ocean, in this case, Chris Pruitt and East Penn, doesn't know any of that.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，大洋彼岸买这批货的人，在这个案子里就是克里斯·普鲁伊特和东彭，对这一切一无所知。

sentences.en: And it's certainly not getting on a plane to go to Nigeria to make sure Trafigura is really engaging in a rigorous audit process.
sentences.zh: 而且他们当然也不会坐飞机去尼日利亚，去确保托克真的在进行严格的审核流程。

sentences.en: So at this point, it sounds like you know the answer to the part of the investigation that you were responsible for from that initial phone call you got about this partnership.
sentences.zh: 所以到这个时候，听起来你已经知道了你从最初接到关于这个合作的那个电话开始，就负责调查的那部分答案。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What about the other question, the question about what kind of medical harm was being caused to the people in these towns in Nigeria by this lead poisoning?
sentences.zh: 那另一个问题呢，关于尼日利亚这些城镇的人们因铅中毒受到了什么样的医疗伤害的问题？

sentences.en: So this is where the examination did an extraordinary amount of legwork.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是《观察家报》（The Examination）做了大量实地基础工作的地方。

sentences.en: So Will had commissioned this team of independent scientists in Nigeria who found 70 volunteers.
sentences.zh: 威利（Will）委托了尼日利亚的一支独立科学家团队，他们找寻了70名志愿者。

sentences.en: And we're talking about 14 children, 16 people who worked at these lead smelters.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是14名儿童，16名在这些铅冶炼厂工作的人。

sentences.en: And these are people who live very close to these smelters.
sentences.zh: 而这些人的住所距离这些冶炼厂非常近。

sentences.en: You know, imagine a village and in the very center of the village, you know, churches right up against the walls of these factories,
sentences.zh: 你可以想象这样一个村庄，村子正中央，甚至有教堂紧挨着这些工厂的墙壁，

sentences.en: schools right up against the walls of these factories.
sentences.zh: 学校也紧挨着这些工厂的墙壁。

sentences.en: So life is playing out all around.
sentences.zh: 因此，日常生活就在这样的环境中展开。

sentences.en: And we tested 70 people, volunteers, right in the vicinity.
sentences.zh: 我们对附近的 70 名志愿者进行了检测。

sentences.en: And roughly 7 out of 10 of them had levels of lead in their blood deemed dangerous by various medical authorities.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，其中大约十分之七的人血液中的铅含量被各医疗机构判定为具有危险性。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So one of the things that we were focused on was this comparison with the worst lead disaster at a battery manufacturer in Southern California more than a decade ago,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们关注的焦点之一是将其与十多年前南加州一家电池制造商发生的最严重铅污染灾难进行对比，

sentences.en: which was a federal emergency.
sentences.zh: 那是一场联邦级别的紧急事件。

sentences.en: I mean, the feds went in, they shut the place down, they tested people, they took over, they're still managing this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，联邦人员介入并关闭了那个地方，他们对人员进行了检测，接管了现场，而且至今仍在处理此事。

sentences.en: And there was a soil test conducted at a preschool there that found 95 parts per million lead.
sentences.zh: 当时那里的幼儿园进行了土壤检测，发现铅含量达到了每百万分之 95。

sentences.en: Let me give you that number again, 95 parts per million.
sentences.zh: 让我再报一次这个数字，每百万分之 95。

sentences.en: We tested a school in Ogie Joe where we found 1,900 parts per million.
sentences.zh: 我们在奥吉乔检测了一所学校，发现那里的铅含量达到了每百万分之 1,900。

sentences.en: My God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At that level of contamination, what kind of health effects would you expect immediately?
sentences.zh: 在那种污染水平下，你预计会立即产生什么样的健康影响？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, you're talking about irreversible brain damage, especially for children.
sentences.zh: 首先，你会面临不可逆转的脑损伤，特别是对于儿童而言。

sentences.en: You're talking about respiratory problems, relentless headaches, exhaustion, just a lack of functioning.
sentences.zh: 你会面临呼吸系统问题、持续不断的头痛、精疲力竭，甚至是丧失正常功能。

sentences.en: And that's the lead, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是铅带来的影响，对吧？

sentences.en: And then there's just the reality of you're living in a place where there's smoke and terrible fumes all the time and people are coughing.
sentences.zh: 然后就是这样一种现实：你生活在一个终日弥漫着浓烟和恶臭、人们不断咳嗽的地方。

sentences.en: It's just a living nightmare.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一场活生生的噩梦。

sentences.en: So what happened after you did all this testing?
sentences.zh: 那么完成所有这些检测之后发生了什么？

sentences.en: After we did the testing, our research partner shared some of this data with the Nigerian government, the environmental authorities.
sentences.zh: 在我们完成检测后，我们的研究伙伴将部分数据分享给了尼日利亚政府和环境监管机构。

sentences.en: And within, you know, just a few days, the five worst smelters in Ogie Joe were shut down.
sentences.zh: 结果在短短几天内，奥吉乔最糟糕的五家冶炼厂就被关闭了。

sentences.en: The heads of these companies were summoned up to Abuja, the capital of Nigeria, to have a conversation around how they could supposedly make some improvements.
sentences.zh: 这些公司的负责人被传唤到尼日利亚首都阿布贾，就他们如何能够做出所谓的一些改进进行会谈。

sentences.en: And then they were given permission to restart.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就被允许重新开工了。

sentences.en: So it sounds like the Nigerian government took pretty swift action.
sentences.zh: 听起来尼日利亚政府采取了相当迅速的行动。

sentences.en: Well, you know, it's complicated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，情况很复杂。

sentences.en: So the Nigerian government has been receiving reports of these health problems going back at least to 2018.
sentences.zh: 尼日利亚政府收到这些健康问题的报告至少可以追溯到 2018 年。

sentences.en: And they got what they described to me as promises to make all of these improvements at these plants.
sentences.zh: 他们收到了他们向我描述的承诺，即在这些工厂进行所有这些改进。

sentences.en: But when somebody showed me a copy of the actual protocol that these factories had to sign, this supposedly enforceable document,
sentences.zh: 但当有人向我展示这些工厂必须签署的实际协议副本时，即这份本应具有法律效力的文件，

sentences.en: it didn't have any of the details of these promises that they claim they got.
sentences.zh: 里面根本没有任何他们声称已经得到的那些承诺的细节。

sentences.en: And it specifically had a two to three year timeline for a very vague promise to improve technology at the plants.
sentences.zh: 并且它具体规定了一个两到三年的时间表，只包含一个关于改进工厂技术的非常模糊的承诺。

sentences.en: So it seems pretty clear that whatever was said in the room with the heads of these smelters,
sentences.zh: 所以很显然，无论在与这些冶炼厂负责人的闭门会议上说过了什么，

sentences.en: there is no enforceable document that compels these companies to do anything differently anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 都没有任何具有法律效力的文件能够迫使这些公司在短期内做出任何改变。

sentences.en: And when I was back on the ground talking to workers at these smelters, what they said is, oh, yeah, now they're giving us safety goggles.
sentences.zh: 当我回到实地与这些冶炼厂的工人交谈时，他们说，哦，是的，现在他们给我们发安全护目镜了。

sentences.en: They didn't used to do that.
sentences.zh: 他们以前可不这样。

sentences.en: Oh, they used to give us gloves once a week.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们以前是一周给一次手套。

sentences.en: Now they're giving them to us twice a week.
sentences.zh: 现在他们一周给我们两次了。

sentences.en: And presumably it's fair to say that the Nigerian government knows that it probably should be doing a lot more than just handing out gloves and goggles if it wants to protect people,
sentences.zh: 可以推断，如果尼日利亚政府想要保护民众，它应该明白，面对检测结果中显示的极高铅含量，它要做的事情肯定远不止分发手套和护目镜那么简单，

sentences.en: given the high levels of lead that is showing up in these test results.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这些检测结果中显示的极高铅含量。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, what has to happen at these plants is they have to put in serious emission controls and it's going to cost millions of dollars if they put in battery breaking equipment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些工厂必须做的是安装严格的废气排放控制装置，如果他们要安装电池拆解设备，这将耗费数百万美元。

sentences.en: That's going to cost millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 那将花费数百万美元。

sentences.en: This is not something that's going to be fixed with a bunch of gloves and goggles.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是靠一堆手套和护目镜就能解决的问题。

sentences.en: I do just wonder, though, given your experience covering global supply chains, knowing what the incentives are for the various actors here,
sentences.zh: 不过我只是在想，鉴于你报道全球供应链的经验，以及你对这里各方利益驱动因素的了解，

sentences.en: knowing how hard it is to reform an entire industry, how confident are you that in five years or ten years or however long,
sentences.zh: 考虑到改革整个行业是多么困难，你有多大信心认为，在五年、十年或无论多久之后，

sentences.en: somebody will be able to purchase a car in the United States and feel confident that the battery in that car was made in a safe and humane way?
sentences.zh: 有人在美国购买汽车时，能够确信这辆汽车里的电池是以安全且符合人道的方式制造的？

sentences.en: I think there are serious reasons to doubt that that positive outcome will happen for the simple reason that the incentives that created this situation that we've been reporting on have not changed.
sentences.zh: 我认为有充分的理由怀疑这种积极的结果是否会发生，原因很简单，即造成我们一直在报道的这种局面的利益驱动因素并没有改变。

sentences.en: And those incentives are you have large brands like East Pen that actually make lots of batteries under other brands.
sentences.zh: 这些利益驱动因素就是，你拥有像东宾这样的大型品牌，它们实际上在其他品牌名下制造了大量的电池。

sentences.en: So it's not as if, you know, a consumer can go off to the to the battery store and say, don't give me one of those East Pen batteries.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是说，你知道的，消费者可以去电池商店说，别给我那种东宾的电池。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: There are lots of others that they make for other brands.
sentences.zh: 它们还为其他品牌生产了许多其他电池。

sentences.en: We also know that Nigeria is hardly alone as being a country where there are large numbers of people who are desperate enough just to figure out how to get dinner on the table tonight that they will accept horrific pollution.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道，尼日利亚绝不是唯一一个拥有大量人口的国家，这些人为了想方设法解决今晚的晚饭问题，已经绝望到愿意接受可怕的污染。

sentences.en: I mean, not that the people in the communities want the pollution, they're horrified by the pollution.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，并不是社区里的居民想要污染，他们对污染感到惊恐万状。

sentences.en: But in terms of the situation for the policymakers, for the environmental regulators, they would like the plants cleaned up, but they're also cognizant that if they push too hard,
sentences.zh: 但就决策者和环境监管机构的处境而言，他们希望工厂得到整治，但他们也清楚，如果他们施压过猛，

sentences.en: this industry will shift somewhere else where some other government will cut a deal with the companies that need lead and other minerals.
sentences.zh: 这个行业就会转移到其他地方，那里的某个政府会与那些需要铅和其他矿产的公司达成交易。

sentences.en: That's how this business tends to go.
sentences.zh: 这项业务往往就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: I mean, my history of looking at supply chain cases now going back decades is that, you know, when you get a public revelation, when you find out that, say,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我研究供应链案例的历史可以追溯到几十年前，当发生公开曝光事件时，比如当你发现，

sentences.en: fashion brand learns that they've been relying on a supplier that's been playing so dangerously that people have died in a fire or in the collapse of a building or rivers or drinking water is being poisoned.
sentences.zh: 某个时尚品牌得知他们一直依赖的供应商运作极其危险，导致有人在火灾、建筑倒塌中丧生，或者河流和饮用水受到污染。

sentences.en: I mean, what tends to happen is the supply chain gets even more complex.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，通常发生的情况是，供应链变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: Pieces shift somewhere else, companies change their names.
sentences.zh: 部分环节转移到别处，公司改名换姓。

sentences.en: Under the guise of safety, perhaps, right?
sentences.zh: 也许是以安全为幌子，对吧？

sentences.en: Like there's consumer pressure and then they say we're going to make these reforms, then the end result is what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 就像存在消费者压力，然后他们说我们要进行这些改革，最后的结果就是你所谈到的那样。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Let's just say for the sake of argument, though, that in this case, in terms of battery recycling, that every player involved wants to do this the right way.
sentences.zh: 不过，为了论证起见，假设在这个案例中，就电池回收而言，涉及的每一方都希望以正确的方式来做这件事。

sentences.en: They want to make a safe battery and make it in an environmentally friendly way.
sentences.zh: 他们希望制造一个安全的电池，并以环保的方式生产它。

sentences.en: What would the increase in cost of that battery to the end buyer actually look like?
sentences.zh: 最终买家承担的电池成本增加究竟会是多少？

sentences.en: Well, it's a hypothetical.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个假设。

sentences.en: It's one that we wrestled with in reporting this story.
sentences.zh: 我们在报道这个故事时也一直在纠结这个问题。

sentences.en: And we concluded that there's no satisfying answer because no battery is going to be made exclusively with lead from one country or another at all basically ends up getting blended together.
sentences.zh: 我们的结论是，没有令人满意的答案，因为没有任何电池会完全只用来自某一个国家的铅制造，所有东西最终都会混合在一起。

sentences.en: But the best we could figure out is you're talking about, you know, pennies on the dollar,
sentences.zh: 但我们能想到的最好估算是，你会谈到，你知道的，九牛一毛的成本，

sentences.en: assuming that every participant in the chain passes on their extra costs to the to the next player.
sentences.zh: 假设链条中的每个参与者都将他们的额外成本转嫁给下一个环节。

sentences.en: You're talking about a single digit dollar number to the consumer at the end of the day in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 最终在美国的消费者身上，你谈论的只是个位数美元的金额。

sentences.en: That's our best guess.
sentences.zh: 这是我们最好的猜测。

sentences.en: There's a lot of assumptions into that, but certainly not a large amount of money.
sentences.zh: 这其中包含了很多假设，但绝对不是一笔巨款。

sentences.en: And I think that it's fair to say that the verdict of the global marketplace on the question of what's it worth to poison entire villages in Nigeria is not that much.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，全球市场对“毒害尼日利亚整个村庄究竟值多少钱”这一问题的裁决是：并不算太多。

sentences.en: Peter, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 彼得，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来，雷切尔。

sentences.en: In the days following publication of the Joint Times investigation, Nigerian officials once again closed down several smelters in the Ogijo region.
sentences.zh: 在《联合时报》调查报告发表后的几天里，尼日利亚官员再次关闭了奥吉乔地区的几家冶炼厂。

sentences.en: Officials also promised new investigations from the federal government and said they would conduct additional blood testing of local residents.
sentences.zh: 官员们还承诺联邦政府将展开新的调查，并表示将对当地居民进行额外的血液检测。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Monday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met for hours with French President Emmanuel Macron in Paris.
sentences.zh: 周一，乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基在巴黎与法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙进行了数小时的会谈。

sentences.en: The meeting was part of a blitz to shore up support from European allies in the midst of negotiations over a U.S.-led plan to end the war with Russia.
sentences.zh: 这次会谈是一系列外交行动的一部分，旨在巩固欧洲盟友的支持，当时正值就结束与俄罗斯战争的美方主导计划进行谈判之际。

sentences.en: While Macron reiterated Europe's commitment to Ukraine, the United States has put increasing pressure on Zelensky to agree to a deal,
sentences.zh: 尽管马克龙重申了欧洲对乌克兰的承诺，但美国对泽连斯基施加了越来越大的压力，要求其同意一项协议，

sentences.en: even as Russia has signaled its opposition to some of the plan's proposals.
sentences.zh: 即便俄罗斯已经表示反对该计划中的某些提议。

sentences.en: And the Transportation Security Administration announced that beginning February 1st,
sentences.zh: 交通安全管理局宣布，从 2 月 1 日开始，

sentences.en: travelers without a Real ID-compliant form of identification will have to pay a $45 fee to fly.
sentences.zh: 没有符合真实身份法案标准身份证件的旅客必须支付 45 美元的费用才能乘机。

sentences.en: Passengers can prepay the fee up to 10 days before they come to the airport.
sentences.zh: 乘客可以在抵达机场前最多提前 10 天预付这笔费用。

sentences.en: Many travelers have already begun flying with passports and other documents considered compliant with the program.
sentences.zh: 许多旅客已经开始使用符合该计划要求的护照和其他证件搭乘航班。

sentences.en: The TSA did not immediately reveal how to pay the new fee and other details about the program.
sentences.zh: 交通安全管理局并未立即透露如何支付这笔新费用以及该计划的其他细节。
